messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 2291-10-01 08:00 UTC - Elevated 5xx and increased latencies for Hosted API & Dedicated pools in eu-west-3. Symptoms: STS token errors, control-plane 502/503 fanout. Paging oncall.

maria.sre: I'm on it — seeing spikes across both hosted endpoints and a few dedicated pools pinned to eu-west-3. Auth errors look like `InvalidIdentityToken` + intermittent 503s from AWS STS.

kevin.infra: Confirming, control-plane telemetry from the node fleet shows a sudden rise in auth failures starting ~2291000008. Also seeing elevated ELB 5xx counts in eu-west-3.

ryan.prodeng: Are we seeing any observability gaps? traces/metrics delayed?

maria.sre: Yes — X-Ray/Trace ingestion to our observability stack is lagging for eu-west-3; Datadog shows partial ingestion errors (500s) at the same window. Could be correlated.

aws-alert-bot: AWS Health: Investigating - AWS STS issuing increased error rates in eu-west-3. Status: Service degraded. https://status.aws.amazon.com/ -> eu-west-3

ops_lead: Paging rotation — @maria.sre primary, @kevin.infra secondary. Sam take customer comms.

sam.support: Noted. Drafting customer status: "We are experiencing elevated latency and 5xx errors in eu-west-3 due to an upstream AWS auth/control-plane issue. We're routing traffic and mitigations are in progress." Will post to status page in 10m.

maria.sre: Immediate mitigations I want to attempt:
- failover routing for Hosted API region tag -> route eu-west-3 traffic to eu-west-1 for non-data-resident requests
- for Dedicated: move affected pools to warm spare pools in eu-west-1 / us-west-2
- enable cached-token fallback for short lived auth (30s TTL) to reduce STS calls

kevin.infra: I can flip the routing policy. Running the rollout plan now. Command to update routing tier:
```
# switch regional preference for eu-west-3 -> eu-west-1
redwoodctl routing update --region-source eu-west-3 --region-target eu-west-1 --weight 0.8
```
Applying conservative weight first.

ryan.prodeng: For Dedicated pools, we'll need a graceful draining plan. Kevin, can we throttle new capacity allocation to avoid double-alloc? Also, set autoscale min to 0 for eu-west-3 pools we're migrating.

kevin.infra: Doing draining in waves of 5 nodes. Drains: 1-5 now, 6-10 in 5m.

maria.sre: Also toggling per-request enrichment (identity lookups) off — that reduces extra STS calls. Patch config:
```
# disable enrichment
PATCH /config/service
{"auth": {"enrichment_enabled": false}}
```
I'll push canary to 10% first.

sam.support: Posted status update to customers (internal copy): "We're routing incoming requests from eu-west-3 to eu-west-1 and applying temporary mitigations to reduce auth calls. Some requests may see increased latency due to cross-region routing. We'll update as we have more info." :loudspeaker:

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager duty escalation triggered for 2291000000. Handoff scheduled in 15m to next oncall.

maria.sre: Observability note: because traces are lagging, rely on internal request logs + ELB metrics. I'm attaching sample error lines:
```
2026-10-01T08:02:14Z ERROR auth: sts:GetCallerIdentity 503 service unavailable region=eu-west-3 request_id=abcd-1234
2026-10-01T08:03:02Z WARN proxy: upstream 502 returning for route /v1/generate
```

kevin.infra: Routing update applied (0.8). Seeing 65% of eu-west-3 traffic now going to eu-west-1. Error rate down ~30% in the last 2 minutes.

ryan.prodeng: We're also enabling model-variant fallback for latency-sensitive endpoints: stateless smaller variants for requests that can tolerate lower quality. This reduces KG of KV-cache pressure and front-end auth calls.

maria.sre: Can we reduce per-request KMS decrypts for embeddings pipelines? Those calls are adding to the fanout.

kevin.infra: Yes — toggled caching for DEK (data encryption key) in-memory for 2 minutes for eu-west-3 traffic. Command:
```
redwoodctl secrets cache --key dek --ttl 120 --regions eu-west-3
```

incident-bot: AWS Health updated: "Service disruption expanded". ETA: unknown. (link)

maria.sre: Next steps: continue draining, finish canary of enrichment off at 10% -> 100% if stable, keep routing weight adjustments. If AWS gives ETAs we'll consider fully failing over.

sam.support: Customer comms update sent. Logged top impacted customers and SLA risk. Notifying account teams.

ops_lead: Reminder — preserve debug logs for any SLA postmortem. Keep an eye on billing for cross-region egress during failover.

ryan.prodeng: If auth stabilizes, plan to rollback routing over 30m. Keep canary options open.

maria.sre: Handing off to next oncall in 12m: @kevin.infra will take lead during handoff. I'll stay reachable for escalation.

kevin.infra: Acknowledged. Monitoring dashboards show error rate dropping, but still elevated vs baseline. I'll keep this channel open for the handoff and update with full mitigation timeline.

incident-bot: Incident 2291000000 - active - severity: high - oncall handoff scheduled. Tags: aws, eu-west-3, auth, routing, dedicated
